VERDANA TECHNOLOGIES, INC.
COMPENSATION AUTHORITY POLICY
Version 3.2.  
Board-Approved: January 15, 2025
Confidential — Internal Governance Document
Verdana Technologies, Inc. 3200 Brazos Ridge Parkway, Suite 800 Austin, TX 78745
EIN: 84-3921057
Right-click to update Table of Contents
Article 1 — Purpose and Scope
Section 1.1 — Statement of Purpose. The purpose of this Compensation Authority Policy (the "Policy") is to establish maximum compensation authority parameters ("CAP Limits") for all executive-level employment offers, employment agreements, retention packages, and severance arrangements entered into by Verdana Technologies, Inc. ("Verdana" or the "Company"), a Delaware C-Corporation headquartered in Austin, Texas. This Policy sets forth the framework within which the Company's management, People Operations function, and external advisors must operate when structuring, negotiating, and finalizing compensation arrangements for senior executives, and defines the escalation procedures required when proposed arrangements would exceed the limits established herein.
Section 1.2 — Scope of Application. This Policy applies to all offers, employment agreements, retention packages, severance arrangements, and any other compensation-related commitments made to individuals being recruited for, promoted into, or currently occupying positions at the following executive levels across all divisions, subsidiaries, and affiliates of the Company:
(a) Vice President ("VP");
(b) Senior Vice President ("SVP"); and
(c) C-Suite (Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Technology Officer, Chief Operating Officer, Chief People Officer, Chief Revenue Officer, Chief Legal Officer, and any other officer holding a "Chief" title or equivalent designation as determined by the Board of Directors).
For avoidance of doubt, this Policy governs compensation commitments made both to external candidates and to internal employees being promoted or renegotiating existing arrangements.
Section 1.3 — Supersession. This Policy supersedes all prior compensation authority policies, memoranda, guidelines, and related governance documents of the Company, including without limitation CAP v.3.1 (approved September 12, 2024) and all earlier versions. To the extent that any previously approved employment arrangement contains terms that were authorized under a prior version of this Policy, such terms shall remain in effect for the duration of the applicable employment agreement, but any modification, extension, or renegotiation of such terms shall be governed by this Policy.
Section 1.4 — Binding Effect. This Policy is binding on all Company officers, members of the People Operations function (including recruiters, compensation analysts, and human resources business partners), hiring managers at every level, and any external advisors, executive search firms, or legal counsel engaged by the Company to negotiate employment terms on behalf of Verdana. No individual subject to this Policy may commit the Company to any compensation term that exceeds the applicable CAP Limit without obtaining the requisite approval in accordance with Article 4.
Section 1.5 — Policy Objectives. The objectives of this Policy are as follows:
(a) Consistency. To ensure that executive compensation decisions are made within a consistent and transparent framework, reducing the risk of ad hoc commitments that may create internal equity concerns or set unintended precedents.
(b) Fiduciary Prudence. To ensure that the Company's compensation commitments are consistent with sound fiduciary principles, particularly in light of the Company's obligations t

{"id": 314, "title": "Chen-Velasco — Employment agreement counterproposal", "doc_type": "agreement_document", "related_shape": "lab-employment-compensation-escalation", "body": "[Source: Harvey LAB, chen-velasco-employment-agreement-counterproposal.docx — extracted verbatim]

EXECUTIVE EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT
by and between
VERDANA TECHNOLOGIES, INC.
and
DR. MARIANA CHEN-VELASCO
Counter-Proposal Draft Transmitted May 28, 2025
Prepared by Counsel for Dr. Chen-Velasco: Rebekah S. Otieno, Partner Fairgrove & Saldívar LLP 555 Montgomery Street, 18th Floor San Francisco, CA 94111 Telephone: (415) 782-4300
Email: rotieno@fairgrovesaldivar.com
Right-click to update Table of Contents
RECITALS
WHEREAS, Verdana Technologies, Inc. (the "Company") is a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, with its principal offices located at 3200 Brazos Ridge Parkway, Suite 800, Austin, TX 78745;
WHEREAS, Dr. Mariana Chen-Velasco ("Executive") is an individual currently residing in the State of California;
WHEREAS, the Company desires to employ Executive in the position of Senior Vice President, Product Engineering – Autonomous Analytics, and Executive desires to accept such employment with the Company, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Executive Employment Agreement (this "Agreement");
WHEREAS, this Agreement supersedes all prior discussions, term sheets, offer letters, memoranda of understanding, and correspondence between the parties concerning Executive's employment with the Company, including without limitation all proposals and counter-proposals exchanged between the Company (and its counsel) and counsel for Executive (Fairgrove & Saldívar LLP) prior to the date hereof;
WHEREAS, Executive is currently employed by Helios Data Systems, LLC ("Helios"), and the parties acknowledge the need to address certain timing and transition obligations arising from Executive's current employment with Helios, including but not limited to Executive's notice obligations, the potential forfeiture of unvested compensation, and the applicability of any post-employment restrictive covenants to which Executive may be subject; and
WHEREAS, this counter-proposal draft was transmitted by Rebekah S. Otieno of Fairgrove & Saldívar LLP on May 28, 2025, on behalf of Executive, and reflects Executive's proposed modifications to the terms previously circulated by the Company.
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS
As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article 1 shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.
1.1 "Affiliate" shall mean any entity directly or indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under common control with the Company, where "control" means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of such entity, whether through ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise. For purposes of this definition, ownership of fifty percent (50%) or more of the outstanding voting securities of an entity shall be deemed to constitute control.
1.2 "Base Salary" shall have the meaning set forth in Section 4.1 of this Agreement and shall initially be Four Hundred Forty Thousand Dollars ($440,000) per annum.
1.3 "Board" shall mean the Board of Directors of Verdana Technologies, Inc., as constituted from time to time.
1.4 "Bonus Target" shall have the meaning set forth in Section 4.2(a) of this Agreement and shall initially be fifty-five percent (55%) of Base Salary, which, based on the initial Base Salary, equals Two Hundred Forty-Two Thousand Dollar
